0cESbNbpYyJtuodHwEBVqA.zh: 德國今年6月迄今報告39例病例,且上一個流行季(2025年6月迄今年3月)累計報告116例病例,其中至少24例住院,全基因組定序顯示,本次流行菌株與歐洲(17個國家)於2011-24年期間疫情(逾600 例)流行之菌株,以及奧地利於2025年檢出之菌株相,疑感染源為義大利進口之番茄,懷疑為灌溉用水受汙染所致。當局警告疫情屬跨年性⻑期流行,且受污染番茄已流入多個歐洲國家。
0cESbNbpYyJtuodHwEBVqA.en: Germany has reported 39 cases since June this year. The previous epidemic season (June 2025 to March this year) reported 116 cases in total, at least 24 of whom were hospitalised. Whole-genome sequencing shows that the outbreak strain is closely related to strains that circulated in Europe (17 countries) during 2011–24 (over 600 cases), as well as to a strain detected in Austria in 2025. The suspected source is tomatoes imported from Italy, with contaminated irrigation water suspected as the cause. Authorities warn that this is a multi-year outbreak and that contaminated tomatoes have reached several European countries.

x71z5bkUYAvBjn_WDGlGPA.en: Germany reported 2 new confirmed cases of Plasmodium falciparum malaria on 17 September, both hospitalised, and one of them died. Neither case had travelled to an endemic area or worked at the airport; they lived in different residences in Schwanheim district, within about five kilometres of Frankfurt Airport. The airport and surrounding area have recorded 8 confirmed cases and 3 deaths so far this year as of 18 September. Germany last reported an airport-related malaria case in 2023. Authorities have reminded physicians to consider malaria in patients with unexplained fever and no travel history.

_O23ZrgT4z3_SBc_TIlw-Q.zh: 全球自2022年截至今年7/31累計145國/地區報告19萬683例確定病例,其中529例死亡。 今年7月共計32國家/地區報告1,370例確定病例,其中7例死亡(CFR:0.5%),以馬達加斯加(703例)、安哥拉(138例)、中國(88 例)、剛果⺠主共和國(55例)及肯亞(55例)為多,74.8%病例來自非洲地區。相較今年6月,全球病例數下降12.5%,僅非洲區呈上升趨勢,其餘地區下降;東南亞區及東地中海區則無通報病例。 全球已有68個國家/地區曾通報檢出Clade Ib確定病例,近6週(7/6-8/16)共有22國報告病例,其中15國出現本土社區傳播疫情,分布於非洲6國(馬達加斯加、安哥拉、肯亞、剛果⺠主共和國、南蘇丹、蒲隆地)及歐洲9國(葡萄牙、德國、法國、英國、愛爾蘭、荷蘭、義大利、瑞士及捷克)。 另馬達加斯加自2025年12月起迄今爆發全球最大規模Ib型疫情。
_O23ZrgT4z3_SBc_TIlw-Q.en: Globally, since 2022 and as of 31 July this year, 145 countries and territories have cumulatively reported 190,683 confirmed cases, including 529 deaths. In July this year, 32 countries and territories reported 1,370 confirmed cases, including 7 deaths (CFR 0.5%); the largest numbers were in Madagascar (703), Angola (138), China (88), the DRC (55) and Kenya (55), and 74.8% of cases came from Africa. Compared with June this year, global cases fell by 12.5%; only Africa showed an increase, while other regions declined, and no cases were reported from South-East Asia or the Eastern Mediterranean region. A total of 68 countries and territories have ever reported confirmed clade Ib cases. In the past six weeks (6 July–16 August), 22 countries reported cases, of which 15 have local community transmission: six in Africa (Madagascar, Angola, Kenya, the DRC, South Sudan and Burundi) and nine in Europe (Portugal, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Ireland, the Netherlands, Italy, Switzerland and Czechia). Madagascar has been experiencing the largest clade Ib outbreak in the world since December 2025.

U6KDJdnwBzrqnJZbLUeMvg.zh: WHO於今年5/14召開第45次IHR小兒麻痺症緊急委員會並於8/25公布決議,今年截至4/30全球累積報告16例WPV1病例、2 例cVDPV1病例、28例cVDPV2病例及2例cVDPV3病例。環境樣本部分:累計報告74件WPV1、27件cVDPV2。考量全球疫情傳播及疫苗覆蓋率,評估持續構成國際關注公共衛生緊急事件(PHEIC),並再延⻑臨時性措施3個月,惟不構成緊急大流行(Pandemic Emergency),並建議有11個國家(有WPV1、cVDPV1、cVDPV3傳播風險者)需加強疫情監測及疫苗接種等措施,包括有WPV1疫情之阿富汗、巴基斯坦、德國,有cVDPV1 疫情之阿爾及利亞、剛果⺠主共和國、吉布地、以色列、寮國,有cVDPV3疫情之喀麥隆、查德、奈及利亞;另建議24個有cVDPV2國內傳播風險的國家加強防治措施。由於核疫區的持續傳播、偏鄉與衝突地區疫苗接種覆蓋率不均以及頻繁的跨國人口流動,WPV1及cVDPV仍具有高度國際傳播風險 。 WHO於8/19宣布非洲5國cVDPV2疫情已終止,分別為蒲隆地 、迦納、幾內亞比索、剛果共和國及烏干達。當局近年透過資金與技術支援、加強疫苗接種,強化急性無力肢體麻痺監測與實驗室檢驗能力,以及應用地理資訊系統的成功阻斷疫情。
U6KDJdnwBzrqnJZbLUeMvg.en: WHO convened the 45th IHR Emergency Committee on polio on 14 May this year and published its decision on 25 August. As of 30 April this year, 16 WPV1 cases, 2 cVDPV1 cases, 28 cVDPV2 cases and 2 cVDPV3 cases had been reported worldwide. For environmental samples, 74 WPV1 and 27 cVDPV2 detections had been reported cumulatively. Considering global transmission and vaccination coverage, the committee assessed that polio continues to constitute a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), extended temporary recommendations by 3 months, but does not constitute a Pandemic Emergency. It recommended that 11 countries at risk of WPV1, cVDPV1 or cVDPV3 transmission strengthen surveillance and vaccination: Afghanistan, Pakistan and Germany (WPV1 outbreaks); Algeria, the DRC, Djibouti, Israel and Laos (cVDPV1 outbreaks); and Cameroon, Chad and Nigeria (cVDPV3 outbreaks). It also recommended that 24 countries at risk of domestic cVDPV2 transmission strengthen control measures. Owing to continued transmission in endemic areas, uneven vaccination coverage in remote and conflict-affected areas, and frequent cross-border population movement, WPV1 and cVDPV remain at high risk of international spread. WHO declared on 19 August that cVDPV2 outbreaks had ended in five African countries: Burundi, Ghana, Guinea-Bissau, the Republic of the Congo and Uganda. In recent years, these outbreaks were stopped through financial and technical support, enhanced vaccination, strengthened acute flaccid paralysis surveillance and laboratory capacity, and the use of geographic information systems.

ZVUSl-BJ_A5pmKiM1wBo-w.en: Europe update: from May 2025 to August this year, 341 confirmed cases have been cumulatively reported, of which at least 34 were hospitalised. The outbreak has risen markedly since May (152 new cases), with patients distributed across seven countries, including the UK (207 cases), the Netherlands (106), Belgium (15) and Germany (6). The UK suspects imported eggs as the source of infection, and the Netherlands suspects chicken meat. Whole-genome sequencing shows that this strain is related to egg and poultry outbreaks reported in the Netherlands in 2025.

Currently, only the country's citizens and nationals, certain government and military personnel, or individuals approved on a case-by-case basis may enter.

jGKYoFtOUgZ4gLWQpheXrA.en: Globally, from 2022 through 31 May this year, 144 countries and territories have reported 185,882 confirmed cases, including 509 deaths. In May this year, 32 countries and territories reported 1,142 confirmed cases, including 3 deaths (CFR 0.3%). The highest numbers were in Madagascar (649), China (89), France (63), Australia (50) and Germany (45), and 63.9% of cases came from the African Region. Compared with April this year, case numbers rose in the Western Pacific and African Regions and declined in other regions. Norway reported its first clade Ib case, and Poland's earlier clade I case has been identified as a clade Ib sub-lineage. In the African Region, over the past 6 weeks (4 May–14 June), 10 countries reported 790 confirmed cases, including 3 deaths (CFR 0.45%). The highest numbers were in Madagascar, Kenya, Guinea, South Sudan, Cameroon and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Outside Africa, Spain and Thailand continued to report clade Ib community transmission. Madagascar has faced the world's largest clade Ib outbreak since December 2025. As of 14 June this year, 2,117 confirmed cases and 7 deaths (mostly among immunocompromised people) have been reported cumulatively. The outbreak has spread to 60% of the country's administrative areas (69 of 115), mainly affecting people aged 15 to 49 years. Although MVA-BN vaccination has been rolled out (more than 79,000 people vaccinated), the outbreak remains uncontrolled because of challenges including vaccine shortages, cold chain logistics and health system capacity.

TNdBRnh0EJcY8A4iGFNsGQ.en: DRC outbreak update: as of 6 June, 515 confirmed cases have been reported (91 deaths, 12 recovered), with a CFR of 17.7%. The outbreak is concentrated in 25 health zones across Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces. DRC's contact tracing rate is about 50.3%. In the past 24 hours, 27 new confirmed cases were added, all in Ituri Province. A US citizen physician who was exposed to infection while performing surgery at Bunia Hospital in Ituri Province, DRC, was treated in a German hospital, including with experimental therapy, and has now recovered and been discharged. The physician was transferred to Germany after 20 May and received antiviral drugs and supportive care. Isolation was lifted after 72 consecutive hours without symptoms and two negative PCR results. Five household contacts placed under precautionary isolation remained asymptomatic.

qKUxc6-Q6_UeTClgmVK8Jw.en: Monthly update: globally, since 2022 and as of 31 March this year, 144 countries and territories have reported 182,945 confirmed cases cumulatively, of which at least 503 died. In March this year, 48 countries and territories reported 1,235 new confirmed cases, including five deaths (CFR 0.4%). 70.4% of cases came from the African region. Compared with February, cases rose in the Eastern Mediterranean and Western Pacific regions and fell in other regions. Colombia, Denmark, Ecuador and Singapore reported their first clade Ib cases. In the African region, over the past six weeks (9 March–19 April), 16 countries reported 969 confirmed cases, including three deaths (CFR 0.3%), with the highest numbers in Madagascar, the DRC, Guinea, Kenya and Burundi. Outside Africa, Argentina, Denmark, Germany, Pakistan, Portugal, Singapore, Spain and the United Kingdom have continued to show clade Ib community transmission. Sindh Province in Pakistan reported a hospital cluster (already known), with transmission mainly attributed to shared incubators and oxygen equipment and contaminated equipment surfaces. In March and April, the province's nine of 30 districts recorded 29 confirmed cases and eight deaths (CFR 28%). All deaths were in infants under six months, and genetic sequencing confirmed a clade Ib variant.

1BlGexCO1199WOmqkA63fw.en: Update. Human cases: this year, 5 H5N1, 12 H9N2 and 1 H10N3 human influenza cases have been reported cumulatively. Most cases had exposure to susceptible animals before onset. Animal and avian outbreaks (WAHIS): 56 countries and territories have reported 3,303 high- and low-pathogenicity avian influenza outbreaks this year. Fifteen countries reported 439 H5N1 outbreaks between 11 March and 30 April 2026: Germany 361, Chile 18, South Korea 14, Poland 13, Nepal 7, France 5, the United States and Taiwan four each, Canada 3, Denmark, Austria, Norway and the Netherlands two each, and Cambodia and Italy one each. SIGR50MKplPxkwHqzYpK_w.en: Epidemic update: In week 11 of this year (16–22 March), the global positivity rate rose to 2.47%, with notable increases in the WHO South-East Asia and Eastern Mediterranean regions. Germany's epidemic is declining and is currently at a low point, with 282 new cases reported in week 13. NB.1.8.1 (68%) remains the predominant variant, while the share of BA.3.2 has risen from 5% in weeks 9–10 of this year to 11% in weeks 10–11. The UK's epidemic has risen slightly, and laboratory test positivity increased slightly to 2.1% in week 13. XFG accounts for the largest share of variants, and BA.3 accounted for 2.13% during 16 February–1 March. Sequencing data in GISAID since December last year show that most BA.3.2 infections occur in young people: 38.8% of cases in the Republic of Ireland and 27% in France were under 18 years, and 49.1% of cases in the United States and 23.4% in Luxembourg were under 10 years, a significantly different age distribution from patients infected with other variants. Assessment and recommendations: XFG currently accounts for the highest share of circulating variants globally (31.44%), followed by NB.1.8.1 (30.68%), and BA.3.2 has risen to 12.5%. WHO's global long-term rapid risk assessment for COVID-19 (9th edition) rates the overall risk to global public health as moderate. Given population immunity from natural infection and vaccination, and advances in clinical treatment, global hospitalizations and deaths have declined markedly since 2022. Most circulating variants are Omicron JN.1 and its descendant subtypes; although they have immune escape capacity, they do not cause greater disease severity, but 6% of symptomatic cases develop long COVID symptoms. COVID-19 has not yet established a stable seasonal pattern, and most countries have reduced routine testing and reporting, so wastewater and sentinel physician surveillance have become important supplementary methods. WHO notes that current vaccines remain effective at preventing severe disease and death, and recommends prioritizing high-risk groups and co-administration with influenza vaccines. Through its Strategic Plan for Coronavirus Disease Threat Management, WHO calls on countries to integrate prevention and control plans, continue strengthening surveillance, protect high-risk groups, maintain health system and public health resilience, and implement risk communication.

This year, as of week 35, 84 countries and territories have cumulatively reported more than 37,000 confirmed cases: African Region 31,980; Region of the Americas 2,825; European Region 1,858; Western Pacific Region 1,067; South-East Asia Region 82; and Eastern Mediterranean Region 33. Since the first case was reported in July 2024, 370 confirmed cases have been cumulatively reported as of 17 August this year, including 6 deaths, five of which were in people living with HIV. Cases are concentrated in Mombasa, the country's second-largest port city in the south-east. More than half of patients are young adults aged 20–40. About 45% of the country's counties (21 of 47) have reported cases. Sexual transmission is the main driver of spread, particularly among truck drivers, sex workers and traders along the main East African transnational highway. China reported one new clade Ib case on 1 August: an adult male traveller who reported symptoms upon entry in mid-July. Authorities launched an epidemiological investigation and preventive measures. Macao reported its first imported case of this year on 27 August, the third case in the region since 2023 (the first two were reported in 2023). The patient is a 29-year-old male Macao resident who developed fever, sore throat and diarrhoea on 23 August. He had sought care on the mainland and returned to Macao for treatment on 26 August, where the infection was confirmed. The patient had high-risk sexual behaviour during travel, but did not disclose the location. Germany reported one new clade Ib case on 19 August: an adult male traveller with a travel history to the United Arab Emirates. Authorities have traced contacts and are monitoring symptoms. Turkey reported three clade Ib cases. One recent case was confirmed in late July and had a travel history to the UAE and Egypt; the other two were retrospective cases with a travel history to Uganda. Authorities have conducted epidemiological investigation and isolation measures. The Democratic Republic of the Congo reported its first two confirmed clade IIb cases. The index case is an adult male with a travel history to Côte d'Ivoire; analysis shows the sequence matches cases in Côte d'Ivoire and Nigeria. Case 2 is a contact of the index case; authorities have traced 25 contacts, 23 of whom received post-exposure vaccination. This is the country's first detection of clade IIb, indicating that clade IIb has entered areas where clade Ia/Ib circulates, increasing public risk. Assessment and recommendations: WHO announced that the long-term recommended measures, originally due to expire on 20 August 2025, will be extended by one year in view of the global epidemiological situation, to prevent and reduce international transmission and its health impact. It emphasizes that continued surveillance, scientific research, community cooperation and equitable resource allocation are the core of global prevention and control for 2025–26. Seven areas of recommendation are: continued optimization of national plans and policies; building surveillance and laboratory diagnostic capacity; strengthening community protection and risk communication; promoting research and clinical trials; formulating travel-related measures (travel bans are not encouraged); providing optimal clinical care and health-worker protection; and ensuring equitable access to vaccines, diagnostics and treatment.

T5o1icBBPBJGiEF_BfKr8A.en: Summary for this week: Human cases: no new human infections were reported this week. Animal and poultry outbreaks (WAHIS): a total of 8 countries reported 52 new H5N1 outbreaks between 17 February and 28 April 2025: the United States 17, South Korea 12, the United Kingdom 11, Germany and Poland 4 each, Hungary 2, and Bangladesh and Denmark 1 each. A total of 2 countries reported 2 new H5N5 outbreaks between 17 March and 11 April 2025: Norway and the United Kingdom 1 each. Japan reported 1 new H3N8 outbreak on 25 April 2025. Avian influenza in US dairy cattle: Herds: since March last year, 1,048 (17) outbreaks have been reported cumulatively across 17 states, with recent cases concentrated in Idaho, California and Arizona. Human infection via cattle: at least 9,300 cases have been monitored cumulatively, 218 tested, of which 41 were positive (conjunctivitis, respiratory and influenza-like symptoms). Other derived outbreaks: infections in domestic cats, sheep, alpacas and others, including a cat death. Wastewater surveillance: in week 17, 407 sampling sites provided test reports, and 5 sampling sites in 3 states (California, Oregon and New Jersey) detected H5-positive results. Other updates: on 2 May the US CDC updated its Influenza Risk Assessment Tool (IRAT), adding two new H5N1 viruses to the assessment list: A/California/147/2024 (genotype B3.13) and A/Washington/239/2024 (genotype D1.1). Both viruses belong to the H5N1 2.3.4.4b clade and were rated as moderate risk, close to other H5N1 viruses previously assessed. A journal commentary published on 28 April by experts from more than 40 countries called on countries to strengthen surveillance, enhance biosecurity and improve preparedness for emerging infectious diseases in response to the H5N1 threat. Since 2024 the US has reported more than 995 dairy herd outbreaks and at least 70 human cases, including several severe cases and the country's first death; some human cases had no contact with infected animals, suggesting the virus may be adapting and may have the potential for human-to-human transmission. The virus also continues to spread among wild birds, poultry and hunted migratory birds, increasing risks to humans and livestock. Continued investment in human and animal surveillance resources, and timely sharing of local abnormal information and viral genetic data, are essential for understanding virus dynamics. Annual summary: Human cases: 10 H5N1 influenza cases (973* cumulative since 2003) and 3 H9N2 influenza cases (131 cumulative); most cases had prior exposure to susceptible animals. (Following WHO counting methods, US H5 influenza cases are classified as H5N1 influenza cases.) Avian and animal cases: 1,656 highly and low pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks have been reported cumulatively by 51 countries and regions. Assessment and recommendations: FAO, WHO and WOAH published a risk assessment on H5 influenza viruses on 17 April. Currently, H5 2.3.4.4b viruses are still avian viruses; most human cases had direct or indirect contact with susceptible animals, and no human-to-human transmission has occurred. Because the virus is widespread in wild and farmed animals, cases are expected to continue, and the global public health risk is assessed as low. For infection risk, the risk is low for the general public and low to moderate for people who frequently contact contaminated animals or environments; the main factors are the mode and duration of contact, protective measures and control measures. Countries are urged to strengthen surveillance of susceptible animals and high-risk groups.

Eight countries reported 23 new cVDPV2-positive samples: seven in Germany, five in the United Kingdom, three each in Nigeria and South Sudan, two in Chad, and one each in Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire and Finland. In Australia, VDPV2-positive samples were detected in wastewater in Melbourne. Testing suggests they may be linked to personnel who received live oral polio vaccine overseas, and the virus continues to spread within Victoria State. Authorities state that vaccination coverage in the area is high and wastewater is effectively treated, and they assess the transmission risk as low.

Ry_nHw8QL-LR7aLPoygsHQ.en: The Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) reported that during 5–11 December, Pakistan reported three new WPV1 cases. Europe has updated its cVDPV2-positive sample information: the United Kingdom reported on 10 December that four positive samples had been detected in London and in the southern and central regions, and Germany reported six new positive samples; all samples were collected in November. Q9axr_PD43jUpEBMKRE9Xw.en: Multiple European countries have experienced an outbreak of Salmonella Strathcona. From 1 January 2023 to 5 November 2024, 16 countries reported 232 cases, with Italy the most affected at 67 cases, followed by Germany at 62. Investigations show that genetic sequencing results indicate the outbreak strains share a common source. Tomatoes produced in the Sicily region of Italy are the possible source, but the actual source and contamination route are still to be clarified.
